messages:
Mira (support): Customer 'AcmePayments' reports a spike of 502s and timeouts since the 09:12 UTC deploy. They say requests intermittently return 502 gateway errors and some timeouts. sample trace id: trace-9a7f2d.
Mira (support): Pasted curl output: `curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -d '{"input":"payroll calc"}'` -> HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway, upstream read timeout.
Leo (support-engineer): I can reproduce a stream of 502s hitting the hosted inference gateway from our probe cluster. 5xx rate on the hosted-api route jumped at 09:12 UTC.
Jorge (eng-oncall): I'm on it. Initial look at routing logs: a non-zero % of traffic was routed to 'canary-pool-42' starting at 09:11:58 due to a staged rollout. Error pattern looks like connection timeouts to the canary runtime nodes.
Priya (runtime): Canaries were supposed to be zero-weight. Who flipped the route override? I see a flag `routing.canary_override` = true in config service history at 09:10:50.
Sam (product): That flag was part of today's staged rollout for the prefetch experiment. We intended 0.1% traffic, not 30%. How did weight jump?
Dan (infra-sre): Autoscale config for canary pool shows `min_replicas: 0` and `burst=false`. If a node receives traffic and it has no warm model shard, cold start + missing prefetch leads to long startup and timeouts, cascade 502.
Jorge (eng-oncall): Evidence: gateway logs show `upstream timeout` and `connect() failed (111: Connection refused)` for canary IPs. Traces have `kvcache-miss` and long model load times.
Leo (support-engineer): Customer impact: some requests time out for 10-30s then 502. Billing is unaffected but UX is degraded.
Mira (support): Customer asked for ETA to fix, they're escalating to their oncall. Need mitigation plan now.
Priya (runtime): Immediate mitigation options: 1) set routing override to false (stop sending to canary), 2) scale canary pool to 3 ready replicas so it can serve, or 3) pin AcmePayments to stable routing group.
Jorge (eng-oncall): I'll cut traffic to canary. Running config change now: `curl -s -X POST https://config.internal/flags -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN' -d '{"flag":"routing.canary_override","value":false}'`
deploy-bot: deploy event: flag routing.canary_override set to false by jorge at 09:28:14 UTC
Dan (infra-sre): Also scaling canary pool just in case: `kubectl scale deployment/canary-runtime-42 -n runtime --replicas=3` (kube job submitted).
Sam (product): We should also audit the rollout automation that bumped weight. Who approved the increase?
Priya (runtime): Patch: the rollout controller had a bug where `traffic_weight` defaulted to env var `ROUTE_WEIGHT` which was set to 30 in the CI job for this pipeline. Fixing controller to cap at max_rollout_pct.
Jorge (eng-oncall): After cutting canary traffic, 5xx rate on hosted-api dropped ~85% within 2 minutes. Grafana: error rate from 12% -> 1.8%. Still seeing a handful of traces from warmup.
Mira (support): Told customer we cut the canary and are rolling back the flag. They asked for incident summary and repro steps once stable.
Leo (support-engineer): Collected traces and a minimal repro: repeat request with header `x-rrid: trace-9a7f2d` to correlate. Provided to runtime team.
Priya (runtime): Root cause write-up: rollout controller misread env var and applied full-weight to canary, combined with canary pool min_replicas=0 and prefetch disabled -> cold starts -> gateway timeouts.
Sam (product): Action items: 1) run a one-off audit check before any staged rollout to ensure min(canary_weight, max_rollout_pct) enforced, 2) set canary pools min_replicas=1 while route override enabled, 3) postmortem.
Dan (infra-sre): I'll open infra ticket to add alert when canary weight > 1% for first 10 minutes of rollout.
Jorge (eng-oncall): Follow-up commands I ran: `kubectl get pods -l app=canary-runtime-42 -n runtime` -> pods healthy after scale. `curl -I https://api.redwood.ai/health` -> 200.
deploy-bot: service alert: hosted-api 5xx rate back to baseline at 09:31:22 UTC
Mira (support): Customer confirmed their requests are succeeding again, thanks.
Priya (runtime): Scheduling rollback of the rollout-controller change and adding unit test. Will patch the env parsing and add caps.
Sam (product): I'll coordinate postmortem and notify the customers affected with timeline + mitigations.
Leo (support-engineer): Adding notes to ticket and sending logs to AcmePayments support thread.
Jorge (eng-oncall): Closing incident. Marking primary mitigations: revert routing flag, scale canary, enforce rollout caps.
Mira (support): Great, I'll update the customer and close escalation. :white_check_mark:
